query: Odile's Last Week Odile Varn finds you between the stacks with her satchel already packed. She leaves at the end of term. "You used the key," she says. It isn't a question. "I won't ask what you found. Unless you want to tell me." Tell her what you've seen She listens to all of it, then puts a hand on your notebook. "Some books want readers," she says. "If one falls open at your feet, don't let it choose you." Then she hugs you, briefly, and is gone. Keep it to yourself She smiles, as if that were the right answer. "Good," she says. "That's how I kept it too." She leaves you her spare candle-stubs and a list of the quietest desks.

The Library to Yourself
The library is yours. No queue for the good desk, no whispering, no one shelving loudly in the next row. Even the librarian's cat has gone off duty, and is asleep on the returns cart.
